title: HIV and viral hepatitis-associated kidney disease

steps.tx: **HIV-associated nephropathy** (HIVAN) is characterized histopathologically by a rapidly progressive collapsing variant of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, accompanied by microcystic tubular dilatation containing proteinaceous casts and diffuse tubulointerstitial inflammation. The image is collapsing focal segmental glomerulosclerosis and microcystic dilatation in HIVAN.

vis.alt: Collapsing focal segmental glomerulosclerosis and microcystic dilatation in HIVAN
vis.caption: Capillary collapse and prominent microcystic tubular ectasia in HIV-associated nephropathy (StewardMD).

steps.tx: HIVAN occurs almost exclusively in individuals of African ancestry carrying two **APOL1** risk alleles (G1/G1, G2/G2, or G1/G2), driven by direct productive HIV infection of podocytes and tubular epithelial cells expressing viral genes nef and vpr. One side is Genetic Susceptibility, and the other side is Viral Pathogenicity.

right.title: Viral Pathogenicity
points: HIV-1 vpr arrests host cell cycle in G2/M

steps.tx: HIV immune complex kidney disease (**HIVICK**) accounts for a major proportion of kidney disease in virally suppressed HIV patients on antiretroviral therapy, presenting with immune-complex mediated MPGN or lupus-like glomerulonephritis without collapsing features. The paired value for Viral viral load is High viremia, CD4 < 200 cells/microL.

steps.tx: **Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate** (TDF) causes proximal renal tubular mitochondrial toxicity via human organic anion transporter 1 (OAT1) accumulation, manifesting as Fanconi syndrome with hypophosphatemia, glucosuria, and declining GFR; substituted by tenofovir alafenamide (TAF). The first step is TDF accumulates in proximal tubule via OAT1.

nodes.label: TDF accumulates in proximal tubule via OAT1

Fanconi syndrome (wasting of PO4, glucose, amino acids)

steps.tx: **Hepatitis B** virus (HBV) is most characteristically associated with secondary membranous nephropathy (predominantly in children and young adults mediated by HBeAg subepithelial deposition) and classical polyarteritis nodosa (PAN). The image is hepatitis B and C viral nephropathies and systemic immune complex syndromes.

steps.tx: **Hepatitis C** virus (HCV) infection is classically associated with Type II mixed cryoglobulinemia, presenting with the Meltzer triad (palpable purpura, arthralgias, asthenia), marked hypocomplementemia with profoundly low C4, and MPGN with intracapillary IgM-kappa cryoglobulin thrombi. The paired value for Meltzer triad is Palpable purpura, arthralgias, severe asthenia.

rows: Profoundly low C4 with normal or mildly low C3
Classical pathway consumption by IgM-IgG complexes
Monoclonal IgM-kappa against polyclonal IgG Fc
Immunofluorescence shows bright IgM and C3 staining

steps.tx: **Direct-acting antivirals** (DAAs: glecaprevir-pibrentasvir, sofosbuvir-velpatasvir) achieve sustained virological response (SVR > 95% to 98%) in HCV-associated cryoglobulinemic MPGN, achieving clinical renal remission and clearing cryoglobulins. One side is Direct-Acting Antivirals (DAA), and the other side is Severe Vasculitis Flares. A key point is Target viral NS3/4A, NS5A, or NS5B.

Well tolerated even in advanced renal failure

steps.tx: COVID-19-associated nephropathy (**COVAN**) is a collapsing glomerulopathy presenting with heavy proteinuria and acute kidney injury in patients with high-risk APOL1 genotypes, triggered by SARS-CoV-2-induced robust interferon-gamma and chemokine release. The first step is SARS-CoV-2 infection in patient with APOL1 G1/G2 genotype.
